steps.title: Deliver control-tower/baselines.yaml: AWSControlTowerBaseline version 5.0 targeting the Infrastructure OU
steps.intent: Deliver control-tower/baselines.yaml at the repository root declaring AWSControlTowerBaseline version "5.0" on the Infrastructure OU with required: true and includeChildrenVerification: true, deriving the version from controlTowerOuBaselineVersion in lza.lock ("5.0"). Per spec section 6.3 and CTCFG-020A, landing-zone version 4.0 pairs with AWSControlTowerBaseline version 5.0; the spec locks this pairing and requires failure rather than silent substitution if the service no longer advertises or accepts it. The file has schemaVersion: 1, validates against deployment/schemas/baselines.schema.json (JSON Schema Draft 2020-12), contains no additional properties, no comments with unresolved decisions, no placeholders, and no duplicate declarations. Infrastructure exists exactly once in config/organization-config.yaml (ARC-004; CTCFG-021). The prototype at inputs/lza-phase0/control-tower/baselines.yaml matches the target verbatim. Note: control-tower/baselines.yaml was placed on main by PR #129 (branch feature/lza-phase0-4-1-control-tower-baseline) before this plan was proposed, with content identical to the target; the schema's additionalProperties: false leaves no additional field to create a distinguishable deliverable. Two matters require operator judgment before this step is buildable: (1) the file already on main has the target content, so the build step is a no-op and build-verify will record action_required for targets that pass on the frozen plan tree (q-already-delivered); (2) AWS GovCloud support for AWSControlTowerBaseline version 5.0 in aws-us-gov / us-gov-west-1 cannot be verified offline (q-govcloud-support). The reserved machinery (.github/**, scripts/**, schemas/**, dashboard/**, root manifests) and governance record (plans/**, confirmations/**, evidence/**, runs/**) are out of scope and must not be touched.
steps.acceptance: control-tower/baselines.yaml exists at the repository root, parses as YAML without error, has schemaVersion: 1, declares a non-empty baselines array with exactly one entry where name is "AWSControlTowerBaseline", version is the string "5.0" (matching controlTowerOuBaselineVersion in lza.lock), targetOu is "Infrastructure", required is true, and includeChildrenVerification is true; the file contains no additional properties; and Infrastructure appears exactly once as an organizationalUnit name in config/organization-config.yaml.

verification_targets.check: control-tower/baselines.yaml exists, parses as YAML, and validates against deployment/schemas/baselines.schema.json using JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 with no validation errors (spec section 6.3; REP-004; CTCFG-020A).
verification_targets.run: test -f control-tower/baselines.yaml && test -f deployment/schemas/baselines.schema.json && python3 -c 'import json,yaml; from jsonschema import validate; validate(yaml.safe_load(open("control-tower/baselines.yaml")), json.load(open("deployment/schemas/baselines.schema.json")))'

verification_targets.check: The version field of the first baseline entry in control-tower/baselines.yaml equals controlTowerOuBaselineVersion in lza.lock; both must be the string "5.0" (spec section 6.3; CTCFG-020A; REP-010).
verification_targets.run: test -f control-tower/baselines.yaml && test -f lza.lock && python3 -c 'import yaml; d=yaml.safe_load(open("control-tower/baselines.yaml")); v=str(d["baselines"][0]["version"]); lock=next(l.split(":",1)[1].strip().strip(chr(34)) for l in open("lza.lock") if l.startswith("controlTowerOuBaselineVersion:")); assert v==lock, repr(v)+" != "+repr(lock)'

verification_targets.check: Infrastructure appears exactly once as an organizationalUnit name in config/organization-config.yaml, confirming the baseline target OU is present in the repository org config (ARC-004; CTCFG-021; spec section 2.2).
verification_targets.run: test -f config/organization-config.yaml && python3 -c 'import yaml; d=yaml.safe_load(open("config/organization-config.yaml")); names=[o["name"] for o in d.get("organizationalUnits",[])] ; assert names.count("Infrastructure")==1, names'

boundary_cases.description: control-tower/baselines.yaml already exists on main (placed by PR #129, branch feature/lza-phase0-4-1-control-tower-baseline) with content identical to this step's target. The schema uses additionalProperties: false, so no additional field can create a distinguishable deliverable. If the build step reproduces the file unchanged, all three verification targets pass on the frozen plan tree and build-verify records action_required — blocking completion. Resolution requires operator judgment on q-already-delivered.

The workload issue requires verifying that AWSControlTowerBaseline version 5.0 is available in the aws-us-gov partition and us-gov-west-1 home region. This cannot be verified offline. If version 5.0 is not available in GovCloud, the spec requires reporting the precise blocker rather than silently substituting another version (CTCFG-020A). Operator confirmation is required on q-govcloud-support.

The baselines schema requires version to be a YAML string matching pattern ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$. Unquoted 5.0 is parsed by YAML as a float and fails schema validation. The delivered file must quote the version as "5.0". The file on main and the prototype both already quote it correctly.

The workload issue asks to confirm a deployment consumer that resolves AWSControlTowerBaseline to an AWS API baseline ARN and Infrastructure to an Organizations OU ARN. That consumer (deploy/scripts/ensure-control-tower-baselines.sh) belongs to Phase 3 and is not delivered by this Phase 0 credential-free workload (REQ-051). Deployability in Phase 0 context means schema-valid and internally consistent, not live-resolvable; the Phase 3 consumer will be delivered in a later workload.
